question.text: A mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> connected to a horizontal spring performs S.H.M. with amplitude <math><mi>A</mi></math>. While mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> is passing through mean position another mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is placed on it so that both the masses move together with amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. The ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>A</mi></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mfrac><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mfrac></mfenced><mfrac bevelled="true"><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math> are the smallest integers. Then what is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></math>?

solution.text:
P.E of the oscillating mass is given by

  E= 1 2 mω x 2 = 1 2 k x 2 where k=m ω 2

Let k=m ω 2 be the velocity at mean position. When mass M 2 is attached v 2 = m 1 v 1 m 1 + m 2

If A 1 be the new amplitude 1 2 k A 1 2 = 1 2 ( m 1 + m 2 ) v 2 2

= 1 2  k A 2 × m 1 m 1 + m 2

⇒ A 1 A = m 1 m 1 + m 2 =14
